page.layout: One column of running text, set in roman and italic with Greek lines. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Marginal notes in the right margin. Catchword and gathering signature at the foot. Left edge shows only the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: longinquius iacere fundam, quàm arcum. In Dione:{4}Lib.xlix. σφενδονῆται μαχοτέρῳ τῶν τόξων ἰόντες, πάντα δὲ τὸν καταφέρ-τον ἰσχυρῶς ἐλυμαίνοντο: Funditores longius quàm sagittarij iaculantes, omnes etiam cataphractos ladebant. Hoc ille in rebus M. Antonij contra Parthos: quos tamen benè armatos fuisse constat, & eosdem sagittis scientissimè usos. Sed praevalebant tamen iis fundae. quod & Xenophon diserte scribit in Graecorum suorum rebus: μαχεστέρως[?] τῶν ψιλῶν[?]Lib. v. Anabas. οἱ τε πολλοὶ τῶν πεζῶν ἐσφενδόνων, καὶ τῶν πλειόνων ἐξοτῶν[?]: Longius enim Rhodij quàm Persa funditores eiaculabantur, atque adeò quàm plerique sagittariorum. Longè igitur ia-culantur: an & certò? Omnes adfirmant, praesertim de Balearibus, & ab infantiâ didicisse destinatos istos ictus.Rectissimè iacul.[?] Quinetiam in Bibliis sacris lectum: Habitatores Gabaa ad septingentos, sic fundis lapides ad certum iecisse, ut capillum quoque possent percutere.Lib. Iudic. cap.xx. De fundis satis, & tu nobis credis? AUD. Debeo. quae frons contra tot talesque testes? tamen praeter fidem opinionemque meam hactenus id esse, non nego. At terrore nihilominus & sonitu Bombardæ vincunt. LIPS. Hoc damus. quid? ut aues terreant? Nam veros milites aut sono aut aspectu illo igneo motum iri, non opinamur: nisi forte in novitate. Et sanè existimo, si Romani primò cum nostris confli-xissent, terrendos sub initia specie & strepitu fuisse: sed sub initia dumtaxat. re perspectâ, futuros qui fuissent. Praesertim qui sic armati, scuto proiecto, leves aut vanos reddidissent istos ictus. AUD. Quid tamen de maioribus tormentis? totas legiones nonne prosternimus? LIPS. Scilicet ut hodie. & periti narrant, nullam aciemTormenta nostra sa-pè inutilia. vidisse hoc telo solutam. Levis colliculus, agger aut margo fossæ interiacens, vim elidit aut directionem ter-ribilis

page.notes: Greek is read with uncertainty in several places (the Xenophon line, its first word, and the last word of the second line); those words are marked [?]. "ladebant" and "Rectissimè iacul." are also doubtful. A faint, illegible marginal note stands in the right margin beside "Debeo" and "tamen praeter" (about 2 words). The sentence "Hoc ille in rebus" is set on the line below "ladebant." and reads as continuous. The reference mark ④ in the text is given as {4}. Speaker names AUD. and LIPS. are printed inline in the running text. Printed "Lip s." is read as LIPS.
